task.description: Root-cause diagnosis and scope recommendation (diagnosis only, not the fix) for ISS-0531: web/src/auth/tokenUtils.ts's resolveTenantSlug/1 falls back to the token issuer realm when the JWT carries no tenant_id claim, applying `realm.startsWith('bpm-') ? realm.slice(4) : realm` -- for the seeded tenant's real realm+slug `bpm-default`, this yields slug `default`, but the tenant's actual slug IS `bpm-default` (slug == idp_realm_id, confirmed live: GET /api/v1/tenants/default -> 404, GET /api/v1/tenants/bpm-default -> 200). AuthProvider.tsx's catch swallows the 404, tenantDisplayName stays null, and every authenticated session renders the literal 'Unknown workspace'. Three options are named, none pre-decided: (a) the prefix-stripping heuristic is wrong, slug should equal the realm (smallest frontend-only change); (b) Letflow should mint a tenant_id claim in the JWT so the SPA never has to guess (backend + IdP config change, removes the guessing entirely); (c) the seeded tenant's slug should not equal its realm (changes seed data / possibly a migration, not application logic). Read web/src/auth/tokenUtils.ts's full resolveTenantSlug/1 implementation and every caller, web/src/auth/AuthProvider.tsx's tenant-resolution flow in full, and check if R-Co had a stated realm/slug naming convention (the heuristic is described as R-Co-inherited) that would inform whether the bpm- prefix-stripping was ever correct for ANY real tenant, or was always wrong. Check lib/letflow/identity.ex's tenant seeding/creation code and any Keycloak realm-provisioning script or doc for whether tenant_id-in-JWT (option b) is actually feasible without extensive Keycloak protocol-mapper configuration work, or is a bigger lift than it sounds. Recommend (a), (b), or (c) explicitly with reasoning, and state which agent role(s) should implement it (FRONTEND-DEV alone for a, or ELIXIR-DEV+FRONTEND-DEV+possibly Keycloak realm config changes for b, or ELIXIR-DEV+a migration for c).
